chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, and a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Saqafi, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, all of them, from Aban ibn Uthman, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, gave Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) the laws of Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, and Isa (peace be upon them): Tawhid (Oneness), Ikhlas (Sincerity), removing the idols, the upright Hanif nature, tolerance, neither priesthood nor wandering, in which He made the good things permissible and the bad things forbidden, and He lifted from them their burdens and the shackles that were upon them.

Then He imposed upon him therein Salat, Zakat, Sawm, Hajj, enjoining good and forbidding evil, the Halal and the Haram, inheritance, hudud (legal punishments), faraid (obligations), and Jihad in the way of Allah. He added for him Wudu, and favored him with the Opening of the Book (Al-Fatiha) and the endings of the Surah Al-Baqarah and Al-Mufassal. He made permissible for him the war booty (Mughnam) and the spoils of land (Fay'), and supported him with awe, and made the earth for him a place of prostration (Masjid) and a purifier. He sent him to all, to the white and the black, to the Jinn and the humans. He gave him the Jizyah, the captives of the polytheists, and their ransom.

Then he was burdened with what no one of the Prophets was burdened with, and a sword was sent down to him from the sky without a sheath, and it was said to him: 'Fight in the way of Allah; you are not burdened except with yourself.'
ai.seo_question: What unique laws and honors were given to Prophet Muhammad (SAW) compared to previous prophets?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi establishes the concept of *Al-Fitrah al-Hanifiyyah* (the pure natural disposition) as the core of Muhammad’s mission, distinguishing it from the asceticism (*Rahbaniyyah*) of previous nations. It highlights the culmination of prophetic law (*Shara'i*) in Islam, emphasizing universality to both Jinn and humans, and unique privileges like the earth as a prayer mat and the 'sword from heaven' symbolizing active struggle. Scholarly tradition views this as a definitive proof for the completeness of Islamic jurisprudence and the finality of the Prophet's message.
